records.name: Gloria Dei (Old Swedes') Church Community Meal Prep
records.summary: Church members and friends who cook a meal every other month for St. Gabriel's Episcopal Church in North Philadelphia, a neighborhood outreach. Anyone can come help cook and serve.
records.what_you_do: Help cook and get a meal ready in the church kitchen on a weeknight evening.

schedule.text: Every other month on a Wednesday evening, 6:30 to 9 pm.

cost.text: No cost mentioned on the event page

first_step.how: Just show up on a meal night, or call the church office at 215-389-1513 or email info@old-swedes.org to RSVP if you can
first_step.basis: The event page invites people to just show up and says an RSVP is optional, with a named contact and general church line.
first_step.what_to_expect: Volunteers cook and get the meal ready in the church kitchen on a weeknight evening, from 6:30 to 9 pm. The meal supports the St. Gabriel's congregation in North Philadelphia, and the page does not list a cost to take part.
first_visit_tips: Tell the church office you are coming if you can, so someone knows to expect you
Plan for an evening trip, since the page does not list parking or transit
Ask what to wear or bring, because the page does not say

records.notes: The event page lists the June 3 and July 29, 2026 dates; it confirms the June date occurred. The church homepage shows the Riverside Hall kitchen used for other church events, but the page does not state Riverside Hall's own street address, so the church address is carried over. The homepage does not describe the meal program beyond the event page. Wheelchair access, parking and transit are not stated anywhere we read.

records.name: Greater Kensington String Band
records.summary: A volunteer string band in Northeast Philadelphia with a clubhouse on Edmund Street. It marches on New Year's Day, plays private events, and welcomes members who do not play an instrument.
records.what_you_do: Play in the band, march, dance, or help as a marshal. Non-playing members are welcome, and the band can teach you an instrument.

schedule.text: Rehearses almost every Tuesday at 8 pm at the Edmund Street clubhouse.

first_step.how: Come to a Tuesday rehearsal at 8 pm at the Edmund Street clubhouse, or fill in the interest form on the join page and a representative will contact you
first_step.basis: The join page says musical experience is not required, non-playing members are welcome, the band can teach an instrument, and the form is one way to reach them.
first_step.what_to_expect: Rehearsals are on Tuesday nights at the clubhouse, and the band has members from teens to people in their 80s. You can join as a musician, dancer, or marshal, and the form asks which instrument you would play if you are a musician. Dues and audition details are not published, so call the band before you come.
first_visit_tips: Call 215-624-9404 before you go to confirm the clubhouse address and rehearsal time
Ask about dues and whether there is an audition before you join
Plan your trip, since the page does not list parking or transit

records.notes: The clubhouse address on the join page is 7235 Edmund Street, but the band's rental section places its hall on Cottman Avenue in the Great Northeast. The two do not match, so the Edmund Street address is carried over and should be confirmed by phone. Dues, audition rules, accessibility and parking are not published.

records.name: Historic Germantown
records.summary: A partnership of about 20 historic houses, museums and gardens in northwest Philadelphia. Its sites offer tours, free events and a volunteer garden program at Wyck.
records.what_you_do: Volunteers at Wyck's Home Farm Club help in the kitchen garden on Tuesdays and Fridays, get short lessons, and take home a share of fresh produce. No sign-up is required.

schedule.text: Wyck garden helpers come on Tuesdays and Fridays. Tours and workshops are held on some weekends in the fall.

locations.label: Partner sites across Germantown, Mount Airy and Chestnut Hill

cost.text: Many events are free. A Cliveden walking tour is $20, or $10 for members and for residents of 19119 and 19144. The Wyck garden program does not list a cost.

first_step.how: Come to the Wyck garden on a Tuesday or Friday; no sign-up is needed. For other questions, email programs@historicgermantownpa.org
first_step.basis: The garden program offers short lessons, needs no registration, and the group's page says so directly, so a beginner can come to a first session.
first_step.what_to_expect: Sessions combine short lessons with hands-on work in the kitchen garden of the historic home farm. Listed morning sessions run from 10 am to noon, and afternoon sessions start at 4 pm. You take home a share of fresh produce, and the page does not list a cost for the garden program.
first_visit_tips: Check the session list on wyck.org before you come, since sessions are listed by date
Wear clothes you can work outside in, because the work is hands-on in a garden
Plan your trip, since the page does not list parking or transit for the garden

records.notes: The garden program's session list (wyck.org) is dated and shows sessions through October 30, 2026; those dates are not written into the schedule text. Wyck's street address is taken from the group's own page. Accessibility, parking and transit for the garden are not stated.

records.name: Interfaith Philadelphia
records.summary: A nonprofit that helps people of different faiths understand each other through talks, classes, community walks, and youth programs. Neighbors can attend the public events or join the newsletter.
records.what_you_do: Go to a talk, take part in the Walk for Understanding fundraiser, or sign up for an interfaith leadership class.

schedule.text: Public programs run through the fall, with talks, virtual classes and a community walk fundraiser.

cost.text: Varies by event; check each registration link. The site has a page titled Slide Scale Fee Structure.

first_step.how: Pick an event on the programs page and use its Register link, or sign up for the newsletter with your name and email
first_step.basis: Each public event has its own registration link and the newsletter form is open to anyone, so a newcomer has a clear way in.
first_step.what_to_expect: Public events are talks, classes and community walks, and many are held in person at Philadelphia sites such as the Arch Street Meeting House or the Rosenbach. Some are virtual, and a few are held as online courses. Costs and how long each event runs are listed on its own registration page, which we did not check one by one.
first_visit_tips: Check whether an event is virtual or in person before you register
Ask about the sliding fee page if cost is a concern
Sign up for the newsletter to hear about new events as they are posted

records.notes: The programs listing has dated events from October to November 2026, which are not written into the schedule text. Several public events are at outside venues, so the address for each event should be checked on its own page. The fall leadership course is virtual and its cost is not stated on the homepage.

records.name: Khmer Performing Arts and Culture
records.summary: A community nonprofit that teaches Khmer (Cambodian) language, dance, and music for free, based at the Preah Buddha Rangsey Temples. It also hosts family events open to the public.
records.what_you_do: Sign up through the class registration form for free language, dance, or music lessons, or come to a public event such as a family day or a community fair.

schedule.text: Language, dance and music classes run on a regular basis. The website does not list class times, so ask the group before you come.

locations.label: Preah Buddha Rangsey Temples community space

cost.text: Instruction is free and the group says it is provided at no cost to anyone.

first_step.how: Fill in the Register for classes form linked on the website, or message the group on Instagram or Facebook to ask about class times
first_step.basis: The classes are free and open to the community, and the site links a registration form, but class times are not published, so the way in is clear but not yet detailed.
first_step.what_to_expect: Classes cover Khmer language and culture, classical and folk dance, and music on instruments such as the khim, takae, drum and xylophone. Language and some dance classes can be taken on Zoom, and most music classes are in person. Class times and the length of each class are not published, so ask before your first visit.
first_visit_tips: Ask for the class time and whether it is in person or on Zoom before you come
Confirm the room, since the site names the temple space as the group's community space but does not list each class location
Plan your trip, since the page does not list parking or transit

records.notes: The group's site has a registration form but no class times, age range, parking or accessibility details. The October 3 2026 health and cultural fair and the November 1 2026 family day are dated events and are not in the schedule text. The site describes accessibility as a value without specifics. The group's contact form hides the email address, so contact is through the form or social media.

records.name: Koresh Dance Company
records.summary: Dance company based at Rittenhouse Square that also runs a studio with adult and children's classes. Its public work includes performances, outreach, and a school.
records.what_you_do: Take an adult drop-in dance class at the studio, such as ballet, contemporary modern, jazz, musical theater, or East African contemporary. Children can join the fall session, and the public can attend the artist showcase.

schedule.text: Adult drop-in classes run Monday to Saturday, mostly 6 to 9 pm on weekdays and late morning to early afternoon on Saturdays. Each class is 90 minutes.

cost.text: Adult drop-in $20 per class, or $19 for students and professionals with valid ID. Class cards: 10 classes for $190 general or $180 student and professional. First-time intro offer: 3 classes for $45.

first_step.how: Call 215-751-0959 or visit the studio to sign up for the 3 classes for $45 first-timer offer, or pre-register online through the class schedule
first_step.basis: The site has a first-timer intro offer and intro and beginner levels, and adult drop-in classes need no membership, so a newcomer can start the same week.
first_step.what_to_expect: Adult classes are 90 minutes and are taught in the studio at Rittenhouse Square. Many beginner classes cover ballet, modern, jazz, musical theater jazz, and East African contemporary. A drop-in class is $20, and the intro offer covers three classes for $45.
first_visit_tips: Pre-register online or call ahead, since the studio encourages it
Tell the front desk you are new so they can place you in an intro or beginner class
Know the studio rules: there are no refunds, and it does not accept American Express or checks

records.notes: Adult drop-in classes are for ages 13 and up. Children's classes exist (fall session), and kids_ok is carried over from tier 1. The adult class page does not list what to wear, studio accessibility, or parking and transit; the studio can be asked directly.

records.name: KyoDaiko
records.summary: A community taiko drumming group that teaches classes to beginners and experienced players and performs at festivals and fundraisers.
records.what_you_do: Take the beginner Fundamentals class, which needs no experience, or join the intermediate class. You can also come to public performances or book a taiko taster workshop.

schedule.text: Fundamentals beginner class meets Thursdays, 7:30 to 9 pm. Intermediate class meets Mondays, 7:30 to 9 pm. Taiko Taster workshops run a few times a year, usually in summer and around the holidays.

locations.label: Practice space (not confirmed on the site)

cost.text: Fees are not listed on the classes page. Ask the group by email.

first_step.how: Email kyodaiko.info@gmail.com to ask about the next Fundamentals class, which needs no prior experience and provides all equipment
first_step.basis: The classes page says no experience is needed and all equipment is provided, and the group welcomes new members, but joining goes through an email to the teacher rather than a drop-in.
first_step.what_to_expect: The Fundamentals class runs 90 minutes on Thursday evenings and provides all the drums and equipment. Ages 12 and up may join, and younger children need a parent supervising. If you want a shorter try first, the taiko taster is a two hour hands-on workshop.
first_visit_tips: Email before you come to confirm the class is running and where it meets
Ask about fees before you go, since the classes page does not list them
Try a taiko taster workshop first if you want a short hands-on start

records.notes: The classes page gives a contact name (Cathi) and the Mondays and Thursdays class times. The practice location is not confirmed on the site: the only address is the footer address, so it is listed as unconfirmed. Fees, parking, transit and accessibility are not stated. The Fundamentals class returns in September 2026 per tier 1, which is not written into the schedule text.
